notes: הַבְאֵשׁ הִבְאִישׁ → 'utterly … made to abhor': infinitive absolute takes the intensifier (rule 56), finite Hiphil the causative frame headed on 'abhor' (rule 44).
'him' of 'to abhor him' kept with the Hiphil as rendering its reflexive sense (David is both subject and referent); the competing reading marks it added.
וְהָיָה לִי לְעֶבֶד: copula on הָיָה, both לְ unrepresented (rules 21, 40), suffix takes 'my', עוֹלָם takes 'for ever' (rule 19).
